notes.text: **[Genesis 28:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.28.11)** — ויפגע במקום וילן שם כי בא השמש ויקח מאבני המקום: “He encountered the place and lodged there, for the sun had set.” The whole os is built on the three clauses of this verse — the encounter (prayer and cleaving), the lodging (the night prayer), and the setting sun (Yaakov himself). *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.10)** — כי בא השמש רבנן אמרי … מלמד שהשקיע הקדוש ברוך הוא גלגל חמה שלא בעונתה בשביל לדבר עם יעקב אבינו בצנעה: the Sages read “for the sun had set” as an early sunset God brought about in order to speak with Yaakov privately, like a king who has the lamps put out to speak with his friend alone. Rav Tzadok uses this first reading to show that, on its terms, “for the sun had set” explains the lodging (he was compelled to stop), which the second reading does not. *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.10)** — רבי פינחס בשם רבי חנין דצפורין אמר שמע קולן של מלאכי השרת אומרים בא השמש בא השמש אתא שמשא אתא שמשא, בשעה שאמר יוסף והנה השמש והירח אמר יעקב מי גלה לו ששמי שמש: Yaakov heard the angels announcing “the sun has come,” and years later, when Yosef dreamed of “the sun and the moon” (**[Genesis 37:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.37.9)**), he said, “Who revealed to him that my name is Sun?” The print's ר"פ is Rabbi Pinchas, as in the Midrash. *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.12)** — רבי שלמוני בשם ריש לקיש אמר תרכוסא של שלש רגלים הראה לו. רבי יהושע דסכנין בשם רבי לוי אמר את הוא רגל שלישי … כי חלק ה' עמו יעקב חבל נחלתו, מה החבל הזה פחות משלשה אין מפקיעין אותו, כך האבות אין פחות משלשה: in the dream God showed Yaakov a three-legged stool, and Yaakov is its third leg; as a cord of fewer than three strands does not hold, so the Patriarchs are not fewer than three. Rav Tzadok reads this as the revelation that Yaakov completes the Chariot, the answer to his question about the angels' “Sun.” *Mafteach: missing*

**[Deuteronomy 32:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.32.9)** — כי חלק ה' עמו יעקב חבל נחלתו: “For Hashem's portion is His people; Yaakov is the cord of His inheritance” — the verse the Midrash expounds as the three-stranded cord of the Patriarchs. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Miketz 12](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Miketz_12) (Rav Tzadok) — quotes the same Midrash (ב"ר פ' סח: מה החבל הזה פחות מג' אין מפקיעין אותו) and explains it as here: יעקב כולל קדושת אברהם ויצחק, citing the Zohar (I 207a) דיעקב תושבחתא דאבהן איהו. It adds that Yaakov's inclusiveness is the attribute of truth (תתן אמת ליעקב), the “threefold cord” that is not quickly broken, and applies it to a Shabbat that falls on Rosh Chodesh Chanukah. *checked*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 47:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.47.6)** — אמר ריש לקיש האבות הן הן המרכבה, שנאמר ויעל אלהים מעל אברהם … והנה ה' נצב עליו: “The Patriarchs are the Chariot,” proven from the same verse Rav Tzadok brings next. He does not name this Midrash, but his “the entire holy Chariot” with “Hashem stood over him” follows it (also **[Bereshit Rabbah 82:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.82.6)**). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 28:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.28.13)** — והנה ה' נצב עליו ויאמר אני ה' אלהי אברהם אביך ואלהי יצחק: “And behold, Hashem stood over him” — in the same verse God names Avraham and Yitzchak, and Yaakov, standing beneath Him, completes the three. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 163b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.38.354)** (Vayetzei) — וְתָא חֲזֵי, יַעֲקֹב אִיהוּ תּוּשְׁבְּחָא דְּאֲבָהָן, וְאִיהוּ כְּלָלָא דְּכֻלְּהוּ, וּבְגִין דְּאִיהוּ כְּלָלָא דְּכֹלָּא, בְּגִין כָּךְ אִיהוּ קָאִים לְאַנְהָרָא לְסִיהֲרָא, דְּיַעֲקֹב אִיהוּ קָאִים לְאַתְקָנָא לִתְפִלַּת עַרְבִית: Yaakov, the glory and sum of the Patriarchs, stands to illuminate the Moon, because he established the evening prayer. Rav Tzadok's daf (קסג ב) is correct; the quotation matches the printed Zohar word for word. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar I 119b; correct: Zohar I 163b)*

**[Berakhot 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26b.4)** — רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: תְּפִלּוֹת אָבוֹת תִּקְּנוּם. רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: תְּפִלּוֹת כְּנֶגֶד תְּמִידִין תִּקְּנוּם: “The prayers — the Patriarchs instituted them,” against the view that they correspond to the daily offerings; the Gemara concludes that the Patriarchs instituted them and the Sages linked them to the offerings. *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.9)** — אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָבוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הִתְקִינוּ שָׁלשׁ תְּפִלּוֹת, אַבְרָהָם תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית … יִצְחָק תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת מִנְחָה … יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם: the Midrash on this very verse gives the three prayers of the Patriarchs with the same proof-texts as the Gemara. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 19:27](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.19.27)** — וישכם אברהם בבקר אל המקום אשר עמד שם את פני ה': “Avraham rose early in the morning to the place where he had stood before Hashem.” Rav Tzadok draws on “in the morning” (בבקר): Avraham's prayer is in full daylight. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Berakhot 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26b.5)** — אַבְרָהָם תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת שַׁחֲרִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם, וְאֵין עֲמִידָה אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיַּעֲמֹד פִּינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּל. Rav Tzadok turns “standing” into a picture: Avraham stood “like one standing directly before the King,” with nothing veiling the light. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 24:63](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.24.63)** — ויצא יצחק לשוח בשדה לפנות ערב: “Yitzchak went out to converse in the field toward evening” — still daylight, which is why Rav Tzadok says Yitzchak too prayed while the light was bright before him. *Mafteach: found*

**[Berakhot 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26b.6)** — יִצְחָק תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת מִנְחָה … וְאֵין שִׂיחָה אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: תְּפִלָּה לְעָנִי כִי יַעֲטֹף וְלִפְנֵי ה' יִשְׁפֹּךְ שִׂיחוֹ. The Gemara's proof-text (“pours out his speech before Hashem,” Psalms 102:1) is the source of Rav Tzadok's “he poured out his speech before Him … and unburdened his whole heart.” *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Beit Yaakov on Torah, Vayetzei 11](#/read/Beit_Yaakov_on_Torah,_Vayetzei_11) (Ishbitz–Radzin) — on וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם, R. Yaakov of Izhbitz says the same of Yaakov: הוּא עִיקַּר הַמְכֻוָּן וּמַטְּרַת הָרָצוֹן שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ … וְכָל הַבְּרוּאִים הֵמָּה רַק בִּשְׁבִילוֹ. He adds the reading of HaMakom from Bereshit Rabbah 68:9 (God is the place of the world) and the image of the first tongs made by Heaven: Yaakov holds the Divine will by which the world is sustained. *checked*

**[Psalms 84:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.84.12)** — כי שמש ומגן ה' אלהים חן וכבוד יתן ה': “For Hashem God is a sun and a shield.” Here “Sun” is a name of God, so the angels' “the Sun has come” gives Yaakov a Divine name. *Mafteach: found*

**[Sotah 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.10a.8)** — ואר יוחנן שמשון על שמו של הקב"ה נקרא שנאמר כי שמש ומגן ה' אלהים: Shimshon (from שמש) was named for the Holy One, blessed be He, on the strength of this verse — the Gemara's proof that “Sun” is a Divine name, which Rav Tzadok applies to Yaakov. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Megillah 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.18a.17)** — מִנַּיִן שֶׁקְּרָאוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיַעֲקֹב אֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּקְרָא לוֹ אֵל אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל … אֶלָּא וַיִּקְרָא לוֹ, לְיַעֲקֹב, אֵל. וּמִי קְרָאוֹ אֵל — אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: God Himself called Yaakov “El.” The words וַיִּקְרָא לוֹ לְיַעֲקֹב אֵל in the os are the Gemara's paraphrase, not the verse. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 33:20](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.33.20)** — ויצב שם מזבח ויקרא לו אל אלהי ישראל: the verse as written; the Gemara reads “He called him (Yaakov) ‘El’,” the One calling being the God of Israel. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Sh'lach 14](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Sh'lach_14) (Rav Tzadok) — Yaakov is “Sun” (citing the same Midrash, מי גילה לו ששמי שמש) and his sons, the Congregation of Israel, are the Moon that receives from him: ובניו הנק' סיהרא כנסת ישראל ומקבלת משמשא. It adds that this happens at the third Shabbat meal and Shabbat Minchah, “Yaakov and his sons rest on it.” *checked*
[Peri Tzadik, Chanukah 17](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Chanukah_17) (Rav Tzadok) — the souls of Israel are the moon that receives light from the sun, and the renewal of the moon is when Yaakov's truth shines on the Congregation of Israel: ויעקב נקרא שמש כמש"נ והנה השמש וא' (בב"ר) מי גילה לו ששמי שמש. It adds that the holiness of Yosef (guarding the covenant) is needed for this truth to enter the heart. *checked*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Beit Aharon, Chanukah 32](https://www.sefaria.org/Beit_Aharon,_Teachings_on_Torah_and_Holidays,_R'_Aharon_(the_Second)_of_Karlin,_Genesis,_Chanukah.32)** (Chassidus) — R. Aharon of Karlin also reads “and he lodged there, for the sun had set” as the hour when the sun goes down into the moon and the moon receives from it, with Yaakov as the Sun (citing the same Midrash). He applies it to the Chanukah lights, lit “when the sun sets.”
ואז הלבנה מקבלת מן השמש ותיכף כשראה יעקב היחוד השלם וילן שם. ויעקב נקרא שמש.
sefaria: Beit Aharon, Teachings on Torah and Holidays, R' Aharon (the Second) of Karlin, Genesis, Chanukah 32

notes.text: **[Berakhot 26b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.26b.7)** — יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּפְגַּע בַּמָּקוֹם וַיָּלֶן שָׁם, וְאֵין פְּגִיעָה אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: … וְאַל תִּפְגַּע בִּי (Jeremiah 7:16). Rav Tzadok explains why the night prayer belongs to Yaakov: prayer in the dark, when the light of His holiness cannot be seen. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sefat Emet, Vayetzei 22](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefat_Emet,_Genesis,_Vayetzei.22.3)** (Chassidus) — the Sefat Emet explains “Yaakov instituted the evening prayer” as the ability to pray wholeheartedly while in distress, so that the troubles themselves flee. Like Rav Tzadok, he ties ויפגע במקום to Yaakov standing in the place of darkness.
וזה מדתו של יעקב אבינו שכתיב ויפגע במקום שהיא ת"ע. כי היה במקום החושך.

**[Bereshit Rabbah 68:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.68.9)** — אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן … בְּעַרְבִית צָרִיךְ אָדָם לוֹמַר יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ ה' אֱלֹהַי שֶׁתּוֹצִיאֵנִי מֵאֲפֵלָה לְאוֹרָה: in the same Midrash on Yaakov's prayer, the evening prayer asks to be brought “from darkness to light.” Rav Tzadok does not cite it, but his account of Yaakov's evening prayer, seeing light from within the darkness, matches it. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Me'or Einayim, Vayetzei 37](https://www.sefaria.org/Me'or_Einayim,_Vayetzei.37)** (Chassidus) — R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl reads the same verse as a person who has fallen: “he lodged there” in a place of darkness from which the light has gone, and “the sun came” (שמש ומגן ה') through “he encountered the place,” that is, prayer and confession. This is Rav Tzadok's point: teshuvah and prayer bring light from within the darkness.
ואחר כך כי בא השמש דהיינו שמש ומגן ה׳ על ידי שויפגע במקום שהוא תפלה ווידוי דברים

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sefat Emet, Vayetzei 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefat_Emet,_Genesis,_Vayetzei.3.3)** (Chassidus) — the Sefat Emet also reads ויפגע במקום as Yaakov cleaving to holiness where the sun's light was absent. He links it to the evening prayer, said in the night of “mixture” (ערב), in which Yaakov found the good point. Through this Yaakov prepared the way, so that no dark place is without his cleaving for his children.
כי בא השמש י"ל בלשון אף ששם לא הי' הארת השמש. אעפ"כ התדבק במקום הקדושה

**[Zohar I 163a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.38.346)** (Vayetzei) — דְּיַעֲקֹב בָּעָא לְאַתְקָנָא תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל עַרְבִית, וּלְאַנְהָרָא לְסִיהֲרָא, וּלְאַשְׁקָאָה וּלְבָרְכָא לָהּ מִכָּל סִטְרִין: on the previous page of the same Zohar passage, Yaakov sought to establish the evening prayer and to illuminate the Moon, watering and blessing it from every side. Rav Tzadok's phrase here repeats the Zohar he cited in paragraph 1 (I 163b). *Mafteach: missing*
**[Genesis 29:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.29.4)** — ויאמר להם יעקב אחי מאין אתם ויאמרו מחרן אנחנו: the shepherds at the well answer Yaakov, “We are from Charan.” *Mafteach: found*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 70:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.70.10)** — רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא פָּתַר קְרָיָא בַּגָּלוּת … מֵחָרָן אֲנָחְנוּ, מֵחֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָנוּ בּוֹרְחִים: R. Yose bar Chanina reads the scene as Israel in exile, “fleeing from the wrath (charon) of the Holy One.” For Rav Tzadok this is the darkness in which Yaakov's night-light works. *Mafteach: found*
**[Genesis 29:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.29.5)** — ויאמר להם הידעתם את לבן בן נחור ויאמרו ידענו: “Do you know Lavan the son of Nachor?” *Mafteach: missing*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 70:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.70.10)** — הַיְדַעְתֶּם אֶת מִי שֶׁהוּא עָתִיד לְלַבֵּן עֲוֹנוֹתֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁלֶג: Lavan (לָבָן) read as the One who will whiten (לְלַבֵּן) sins like snow. The Midrash echoes **[Isaiah 1:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.1.18)**, אם יהיו חטאיכם כשנים כשלג ילבינו. Rav Tzadok ends on this: even from within the exile's darkness, teshuvah can remove the darkness and lead to great light. *Mafteach: found*

connector.why: Shares Genesis 28:11 and the arvit derashah only; its theme (Yaakov going out in safety, the Midrash on "az telech lavetach") is different. Not used.
Same Midrash (mi gilah lo she-shmi shemesh): Yaakov = sun, Knesses Yisrael = moon receiving from him. Used.
Same Midrash on chevel nachalaso (fewer than three strands) and Yaakov as the sum of the Avos (Zohar I 207a). Used.
From the Mafteach lead on BR 68:10. Yaakov the sun renews the moon (Knesses Yisrael). Used.
Ishbitz–Radzin: on Vayifga baMakom, Yaakov is the purpose of creation (= 2.26). Used.
The Mafteach lists it under Genesis 28:11–13, but it concerns Amalek and imagination; it shares only the dream verse. Not used.

found.why: Vayalen sham = a place of darkness; ki va hashemesh = shemesh u-magen through vayifga (prayer and viduy). The same move from darkness to light through teshuvah and prayer.
Vayifga = cleaving to holiness where there was no sunlight; arvit = finding the good point in the night.
Arvit = praying wholeheartedly in distress; Yaakov was "in the place of darkness".

found.why: Ki va hashemesh = the sun goes into the moon, which receives from it; Yaakov called Sun (same Midrash).

corrections.quote: וְאִיתָא בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (קסג עַמּוּד ב): וְתָא חֲזֵי, יַעֲקֹב תּוּשְׁבְּחָא דַּאֲבָהָן
corrections.note: He cites 163b and quotes Zohar, Vayetzei 38:14 (163b). The 119b phrase (Vayera 33:4, "תושבחן דאבהן יעקב הוה") is a different passage.
Avraham and Shacharit; verse quoted unnamed
